background.fact: Adobe developed EPS in the late 1980s for placing illustrations in printed documents.
An EPS represents one rectangular graphic through PostScript instructions.
The format can combine vector drawing commands with raster images.
EPS version 3 appeared in 1990; Adobe published its separate specification in 1992.
The MIME type is application/postscript.
PDF has replaced EPS in many publishing workflows, though EPS remains relevant to legacy artwork.

windows.note: Reads EPS through Ghostscript; installed policy and delegates determine availability.
Interprets the PostScript instructions used by EPS.
Can open EPS or place it as linked artwork; unfamiliar objects can be lost during import.

mac.note: Reads EPS through Ghostscript; installed policy and delegates determine availability.
Interprets the PostScript instructions used by EPS.
Can open EPS or place it as linked artwork; unfamiliar objects can be lost during import.

linux.note: Reads EPS through Ghostscript; installed policy and delegates determine availability.
Interprets the PostScript instructions used by EPS.

problems.fact: Current macOS lacks a built-in EPS viewer; Preview support is limited to older releases such as macOS 12 and earlier.
EPS cannot retain live transparency; Adobe recommends PDF 1.4 when placing transparent artwork.
Opening an EPS in Illustrator can discard objects that its importer does not recognize.
ImageMagick needs Ghostscript to decode EPS, so an installation without it cannot render the artwork.

background.fact: AVCHD is a camera recording system that packages its streams as MPEG-2 Transport Stream.
Its standard video compression uses MPEG-4 AVC/H.264.
Audio may use Dolby Digital AC-3 or uncompressed Linear PCM.
The recording system includes interlaced and progressive HD modes.
The published format includes 8-bit samples with 4:2:0 chroma sampling.
AVCHD recording media include memory cards, built-in storage and 8 cm DVD media.

windows.note: Can read MPEG transport streams and decode H.264 camera clips; this does not promise reconstruction of camera menus.
Reads MPEG-TS and H.264 streams for inspection and conversion of camera clips.

mac.note: Can read MPEG transport streams and decode H.264 camera clips; this does not promise reconstruction of camera menus.
Reads MPEG-TS and H.264 streams for inspection and conversion of camera clips.
Sony documents AVCHD PS-mode import with iMovie 10 and OS X 10.9 or later.

linux.note: Can read MPEG transport streams and decode H.264 camera clips; this does not promise reconstruction of camera menus.
Reads MPEG-TS and H.264 streams for inspection and conversion of camera clips.

problems.fact: Abrupt changes in brightness or camera angle can make compressed AVCHD pictures look unstable without indicating a camera fault.
iMovie 08, 09 and 11 do not support AVCHD 2.0 recordings made in 1080/60p or 720/60p.
Importing 50p or 60p AVCHD PS-mode footage into iMovie requires iMovie 10 or later and OS X 10.9 or later.

background.fact: The .oga extension identifies general Ogg audio rather than a single audio codec.
RFC 5334 registered audio/ogg and its .oga extension in September 2008.
A .ogg extension is reserved by that RFC for Ogg containing a Vorbis-only bitstream.
An Ogg audio stream can carry different codecs, including Vorbis, FLAC and Speex.
The Xiph.Org Foundation controls the audio/ogg registration.
Ogg files begin with an OggS capture pattern.

windows.note: Opens Ogg containers; playback also depends on the enclosed codec.
Demuxes Ogg and decodes supported Vorbis, FLAC, Speex and Opus audio.

mac.note: Opens Ogg containers; playback also depends on the enclosed codec.
Demuxes Ogg and decodes supported Vorbis, FLAC, Speex and Opus audio.

linux.note: Opens Ogg containers; playback also depends on the enclosed codec.
Demuxes Ogg and decodes supported Vorbis, FLAC, Speex and Opus audio.

mobile.note: Its publisher lists Ogg container support with included decoders.

problems.fact: A player that recognizes the Ogg wrapper can still lack the decoder for the particular audio stream.
Treating every .oga as Vorbis misidentifies files encoded with other audio codecs.
A codec-specific .ogg assumption can prevent an application from handling general .oga streams correctly.

background.fact: Microsoft created ASF as a proprietary, publicly documented multimedia wrapper.
An ASF can hold audio, video, still images and other stream types.
WMA and WMV are ASF subtypes associated with Windows Media streams.
ASF was designed for media delivery, including streaming.
Header objects can carry titles, authorship, copyright and technical metadata.
Its registered MIME type is application/vnd.ms-asf.

windows.note: Lists ASF, WMV and WMA among its input formats.
Supports ASF input and output; supported stream decoders are still required.

mac.note: Lists ASF, WMV and WMA among its input formats.
Supports ASF input and output; supported stream decoders are still required.

linux.note: Lists ASF, WMV and WMA among its input formats.
Supports ASF input and output; supported stream decoders are still required.

problems.fact: The ASF extension identifies a wrapper, so it does not establish which audio or video decoder is needed.
Picture fidelity and multichannel support depend on the encoded streams rather than the ASF wrapper.
ASF metadata can include digital rights management information, which must not be mistaken for ordinary descriptive tags.

background.fact: DICOM defines medical objects including images, waveforms, reports and related information.
The registered MIME type for DICOM files is application/dicom.
The registration recommends .dcm for disk files other than DICOMDIR.
DICOMDIR can index a collection of related DICOM files.
DICOM files use binary information and require lossless binary transfer.
A DICM marker following a 128-byte preamble identifies the Part 10 file structure.
The ACR-NEMA predecessor appeared in 1985; the renamed DICOM standard followed in 1993.

windows.note: Windows viewer, free for noncommercial use, for CT, MRI and other DICOM studies.
Imports DICOM studies into a database, then loads the chosen series; extra objects may need extensions.
Reads DICOM images and recognizes window center and width tags; it is not a full study-management viewer.

mac.note: Imports DICOM studies into a database, then loads the chosen series; extra objects may need extensions.
Reads DICOM images and recognizes window center and width tags; it is not a full study-management viewer.

linux.note: Imports DICOM studies into a database, then loads the chosen series; extra objects may need extensions.
Reads DICOM images and recognizes window center and width tags; it is not a full study-management viewer.

problems.fact: Opening one instance may show only one slice because an image series often spans many files.
Some DICOM information objects require Slicer extensions instead of its core image importer.
File and folder names do not reliably identify the patient, study or series; use the DICOM attributes.
DICOM objects can contain demographic information, so sharing an exported image and sharing the source study have different privacy consequences.

background.fact: PPT is the binary presentation format used by PowerPoint 97 through Office 2003.
The .ppt extension differs from the later XML-based .pptx format.
A presentation holds slides, which can include text, graphics, transitions and animations.
The presentation model also supports notes, handouts and comments.
The MIME type is application/vnd.ms-powerpoint.
PPT cannot represent every feature introduced in PowerPoint 2007 and later.

windows.note: Opens .ppt and .pps through File > Open.
Imports legacy PPT presentations and can save in PowerPoint format.
Opens legacy PowerPoint 97-2003 presentations; newer features may require PPTX.

mac.note: Opens .ppt and .pps through File > Open.
Imports legacy PPT presentations and can save in PowerPoint format.
Opens legacy PowerPoint 97-2003 presentations; newer features may require PPTX.

linux.note: Imports legacy PPT presentations and can save in PowerPoint format.

web.note: Reads PPT; save a copy as PPTX to edit it.
Imports Microsoft PowerPoint presentations into the browser editor.

problems.fact: Saving newer presentation features into PPT can lose functionality that the older format cannot store.
PowerPoint for the web reads .ppt but requires a .pptx copy for editing.
A file downloaded from the internet may be blocked by Office security and report that it cannot be opened.

background.fact: Autodesk publishes DXF to exchange AutoCAD drawing data.
The first DXF documentation appeared in 1982.
DXF exists in text and binary representations.
A text DXF uses group codes paired with values.
New drawing capabilities have introduced additional codes and format versions.
The registered MIME type is image/vnd.dxf.

windows.note: Reads DXF drawings in its 2D CAD workspace.
Free 2D CAD application with DXF support; advanced interchange features belong to QCAD Professional.
Imports DXF from AutoCAD 2.5 through 2007, with unit and scale settings.
Use Open Drawing and select DXF in the file-type list.

mac.note: Reads DXF drawings in its 2D CAD workspace.
Free 2D CAD application with DXF support; advanced interchange features belong to QCAD Professional.
Imports DXF from AutoCAD 2.5 through 2007, with unit and scale settings.

linux.note: Reads DXF drawings in its 2D CAD workspace.
Free 2D CAD application with DXF support; advanced interchange features belong to QCAD Professional.

web.note: Autodesk offers browser viewing for CAD interchange files including DXF.

problems.fact: LibreCAD does not implement every DXF feature and lists supported versions through DXF 2007.
Illustrator refuses AutoCAD drawings saved later than the 2007 format; an older export is needed.
An Illustrator DXF import can ask for missing external references because the drawing points to separate files.
Scale and unit mapping need attention when moving a CAD drawing into Illustrator.

background.fact: JP2 wraps a JPEG 2000 codestream in the Part 1 file format.
The Joint Photographic Experts Group developed this still-image wrapper.
JPEG 2000 compression can be lossy or lossless.
The wrapper can store color profiles, opacity information and other metadata.
Its standard extension is .jp2 and its registered media type is image/jp2.
The Library of Congress uses lossy JP2 service images for digitized maps and newspapers.

windows.note: Lists read and write support for JP2; check the installed format list for a particular build.
Open-source JPEG 2000 codec and command-line utilities; decoding support is distinct from an interactive viewer.
Adobe documents opening JP2 images in Photoshop.

mac.note: Lists read and write support for JP2; check the installed format list for a particular build.
Open-source JPEG 2000 codec and command-line utilities; decoding support is distinct from an interactive viewer.
Adobe documents opening JP2 images in Photoshop.

linux.note: Lists read and write support for JP2; check the installed format list for a particular build.
Open-source JPEG 2000 codec and command-line utilities; decoding support is distinct from an interactive viewer.

problems.fact: A JP2 is not interchangeable with a JPX file: JPX belongs to JPEG 2000 Part 2 rather than the basic Part 1 wrapper.
A lossy JPEG 2000 codestream does not recover discarded image information simply by being saved as JP2.

background.fact: AV1 means AOMedia Video 1 and identifies a video codec rather than a complete multimedia container.
The Alliance for Open Media developed its bitstream and decoding specification.
AV1 is an open, royalty-free video coding format.
Its bitstream is organized into open bitstream units called OBUs.
Its registered media type is video/av1.
AV1 supports full-resolution chroma configurations, including 4:4:4.
AOMedia announced the public release of the AV1 1.0 specification on March 28, 2018.

windows.note: Can decode AV1 through documented decoders; build options determine available implementations.
FFmpeg-based test player.

mac.note: Can decode AV1 through documented decoders; build options determine available implementations.
FFmpeg-based test player.

linux.note: Can decode AV1 through documented decoders; build options determine available implementations.

problems.fact: AV1 has no required filename extension, so the suffix alone cannot establish the container or framing.
AV1 encoding can take longer because the compression process is complex.
A raw OBU stream and an AV1 image container are different inputs; FFmpeg documents them as separate formats.
